title: Where to look for a job in Germany
description: The job portals and platforms that work for international candidates, how to choose the right ones and how to use them without drowning in listings.
html:
There are more job platforms in Germany than anyone can use, and newcomers often spread themselves across all of them. A better approach is to pick a handful that fit your field and use them well. Here is how the landscape looks.

General platforms

The large international networks and the big German job boards list the widest range of positions. The Federal Employment Agency runs the largest public portal, with listings from every sector and a large share of jobs outside the big cities. Aggregators pull listings from company sites and are useful for a quick overview, though they contain duplicates.

Specialised platforms

Tech roles cluster on developer-focused boards and start-up job sites, where English-language listings are common. Engineering and manufacturing jobs appear on industry portals run by professional associations. Academic and research positions have their own boards linked to universities and institutes. English-only job boards for international candidates exist and are worth checking, although the volume is lower.

Company career pages

Large employers post first on their own sites, and some roles never reach the portals. Make a list of 20 to 30 companies in your field and check their career pages directly, or set up alerts.

How to choose

Pick one general platform, one or two specialised ones and the career pages of your target companies. Set up alerts with precise keywords and locations so that new listings come to you. Ignore the rest; more platforms means more noise, not more offers.

Using them well

Complete your profile in full; recruiters search profiles as often as candidates search jobs. Apply within the first days of a listing going live. Tailor the CV to each application, even slightly. Track what you send in a simple spreadsheet. And treat the search as work: a fixed block of hours each day produces far more than checking listings at random.
